metadata.name: Finance Type
metadata.description: DAC/CRS transaction classification used to distinguish financial instruments,  e.g. grants or loans.

data.name: Standard grant
data.description: Grants are transfers in cash or in kind for which no legal debt is incurred by the recipient.

data.name: Individual loan guarantee
data.description: A guarantee on an individual standard loan

data.name: Loan portfolio guarantee
data.description: A guarantee covering a portfolio of standard loans administered by financial intermediaries, such as banks, microfinance institutions or collective investment vehicles.

data.name: Individual mezzanine finance guarantee
data.description: A guarantee on an individual mezzanine finance investment (subordinated loans or preferred equities).

data.name: Mezzanine finance portfolio guarantee
data.description: A guarantee covering a portfolio of mezzanine finance investments (subordinated loans or preferred equities) administered by financial intermediaries, such as banks, microfinance institutions or collective investment vehicles.

data.name: Individual equity finance guarantee
data.description: A guarantee covering an equity investment.

data.name: Equity portfolio guarantee
data.description: A guarantee covering a portfolio of equity investments administered by financial intermediaries, such as banks, microfinance institutions or collective investment vehicles.

data.name: First-loss guarantee
data.description: A guarantee specifically designed to absorb the very first loss on one or more investments, such as in the context of collective investment vehicles. Please use other codes for guarantees that are not specifically designed to absorb the very first loss.

data.name: Other guarantees
data.description: Other guarantees, such as volume guarantees, payment guarantees etc.

data.name: INTEREST SUBSIDY
data.description: Subsidies to soften the terms of private export credits, or loans or credits by the banking sector.

data.name: Interest subsidy
data.description: A payment to soften the terms of private export credits, or loans or credits by the banking sector.

data.name: Interest subsidy to national private exporters
CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION
data.description: Payments to multilateral agencies in the form of notes and similar instruments, unconditionally cashable at sight by the recipient institutions.

data.name: Capital subscription on deposit basis
data.description: Payments to multilateral agencies in the form of notes and similar instruments, unconditionally encashable at sight by the recipient institutions.

data.name: Subsidies and similar transfers
data.description: This category includes subsidies and social benefits to households as defined in the System of National Accounts (SNA). Subsidies are unrequited payments that government units, including non-resident government units, make to enterprises on the basis of the levels of their production activities or the quantities or values of the goods or services which they produce, sell or import. Subsidies prohibited by the WTO are not reportable in TOSSD. Social benefits to households are current transfers received by households that are intended to provide for the needs that arise from certain events or circumstances, for example housing. Subsidies and similar transfers can be used by governments to promote sustainable development objectives, for example by supporting research activities carried out by pharmaceutical firms or efforts by households to improve the energy efficiency of their housing. According to the United Nations System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA), an environmental subsidy or similar transfer is a transfer intended to support activities that protect the environment or reduce the use and extraction of natural resources.

data.name: Capital subscription on encashment basis
data.description: Payments to multilateral agencies in the form of notes and similar instruments, unconditionally encashable at sight by the recipient institutions.

data.name: LOAN
data.description: Transfers in cash or in kind for which the recipient incurs legal debt.

data.name: Loan in a joint venture with the recipient
Standard loan
data.description: Transfers in cash or in kind for which the recipient incurs legal debt (and the resulting claim is not intended to be traded). Since payment obligations on standard loan are senior obligations, i.e. creditors are entitled to receive payments against their claims before anyone else, they are also referred to as senior loans.

data.name: Reimbursable grant
data.description: A contribution provided to a recipient institution for investment purposes, with the expectation of long-term reflows at conditions specified in the financing agreement. The provider assumes the risk of total or partial failure of the investment; it can also decide if and when to reclaim its investment.

data.name: Loan-type reimbursable grant
data.description: A contribution provided to a recipient institution for investment purposes, for which the conditions - including a concrete repayment schedule – are specified in the financing agreement.

data.name: Reflow-based reimbursable grant
data.description: A contribution provided to a recipient institution for investment purposes, for which the details on reflows are unknown at the time of investment as they depend on the performance of the underlying investments.

data.name: Bonds
data.description: Fixed-interest debt instruments, issued by governments, public utilities, banks or companies, tradable in financial markets.

data.name: Asset-backed securities
data.description: Securities whose value and income payments are derived from and backed by a specific pool of underlying assets.

data.name: Subordinated loan
data.description: A loan that, in the event of default, will only be repaid after all senior obligations have been satisfied. In compensation for the increased risk, mezzanine debt holders require a higher return for their investment than secured or more senior lenders.

data.name: Preferred equity
data.description: Equity that, in the event of default, will be repaid after all senior obligations and subordinated loans have been satisfied; and will be paid before common equity holders. It is a more expensive source of finance than senior debt, a less expensive source than equity.

data.name: Other hybrid instruments
data.description: Including convertible debt or equity.

data.name: Multilateral hybrid capital
data.description: Hybrid capital instruments issued by multilateral institutions

data.name: Non-banks non-guaranteed portions of guaranteed export credits
Common equity
data.description: A share in the ownership of a corporation that gives the owner claims on the residual value of the corporation after creditors’ claims have been met.

data.name: Acquisition of equity not part of joint venture in developing countries
Shares in collective investment vehicles
data.description: Collective undertakings through which investors pool funds for investment in financial or nonfinancial assets or both. These vehicles issue shares (if a corporate structure is used) or units (if a trust structure is used).

data.name: Reinvested earnings
data.description: This item is only applicable to Foreign Direct Investment (FDI). Reinvested earnings on FDI consist of the retained earnings of a direct foreign investment enterprise which are treated as if they were distributed and remitted to foreign direct investors in proportion to their ownership of the equity of the enterprise and then reinvested by them in the enterprise.

data.name: Debt rescheduling: OOF claim (DSR – original loan principal)
Debt rescheduling: OOF claim (DSR – original loan interest)
Debt rescheduling: Private claim (DSR – original loan principal)
Debt rescheduling: export credit claim (DSR – original loan principal)
INVESTMENT
data.description: Investment made by a private entity resident in a reporting country to acquire or add to a lasting interest(1) in an enterprise in a country on the DAC List of ODA Recipients.

data.name: Foreign direct investment, new capital outflow (includes reinvested earnings if separate identification not available)
Other foreign direct investment, including reinvested earnings

data.description: Acquisition of bonds issued by developing countries.

Securities and other instruments originally issued by multilateral agencies
